rationale: Demonstrative ⲡⲓ- + ⲍⲙⲁⲧ (= Sahidic ⲥⲙⲟⲧ 'form, fashion, manner'). Direct equivalent of ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ already in glossary. Used in dialogue formula 'doing for him in this manner' (line 2). Confirms the ⲥⲙⲟⲧ root with Lyc ⲍ-onset, paralleling other ⲍ-for-ϩ/ⲥ shifts.

Apparent reduplicated qualitative; etymology unclear. Possibly cognate with ⲗⲁⲕⲗⲱⲕ 'soft, gentle' (Crum) extended to mean 'weakened, exhausted' in bodily context. Stands in triadic series with ⲯⲱⲛⲉ 'sick' and ⲫⲗⲓⲃⲉ 'oppressed' as progressive somatic decline.

Disability/injury noun in negative-existential phrase ⲉⲙⲛ̄ ⲭⲃⲓⲛ 'with no harm.' Possibly Lyc reflex of ϫⲃⲓⲛ 'lameness, deficiency' or related to ϭⲃⲃⲉ 'be weak.' Forms doublet with ⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'destruction' and ϯⲕⲉⲥ 'affliction.' Confidence low.
Qualitative of Coptic ⲣⲟⲟⲩⲧ 'be ready, prepared, joyful' (Crum 309b). Used circumstantially: ⲉⲕⲣⲁⲩⲧ 'you being eager' — the disciple's bold readiness in proclaiming his (mistaken) view.

Obscure predicative form. Tentatively analyzed as ⲛ̄- (predicate-of) + ⲧⲃⲁⲧ from a root meaning 'spit, despise' (cf. Crum ⲧⲃⲏⲧ 'spittle/contempt'). Used of the entire profit being nullified by the disciple's refusal. Could alternatively reflect a 'go-to-naught' verb. Flag for parallels.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧⲁⲛϩⲟⲩⲧ 'entrust' + 2sg suffix. With directional ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'to it' = 'entrusted to it/the work.' The Manichaean apostolic register of being commissioned to a divine task.

Indefinite article ⲟⲩ- + ⲟⲣⲟ (Lyc for ⲡⲟⲣⲟ = ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'king/kingship'); cf. ⲡⲟⲣⲟ in accumulated vocabulary. Used in formulaic doublet with ⲉⲁⲩ 'glory' for the eschatological reward of the faithful disciple entering the land of rest.

Lycopolitan qualitative of ⲟⲩⲱⲡ/ⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ 'be holy, pure' with regular ⲃ→ⲭ shift. Predicates the disciple's body in eschatological declaration: 'your body is holy unto you' — i.e., preserved intact through fidelity to the entrusted work.
